sources.title: Releasing Claude Instant 1.2
sources.evidence: Dated August 9, 2023; announces version 1.2 availability through the paid API, names predecessor Instant 1.1, and describes text tasks and response improvements. No parameter counts or architecture are specified.

sources.title: Prompt engineering for Claude's long context window
sources.evidence: September 23, 2023 article introduces the 100,000-token context window and explicitly identifies Instant 1.2 as the evaluated model, including tests with 70K and 95K token documents and text answers.

sources.title: Model deprecations
sources.evidence: Exact claude-instant-1.2 identifier appears in the September 4, 2024 deprecation group, with November 6, 2024 retirement. The page distinguishes Anthropic platform retirement from partner-operated platforms.

sources.title: Model Card and Evaluations for Claude Models (original Claude 2 card)
sources.evidence: Page 1 describes Claude 2 and previous Claude models as using a Transformer; page 3 explicitly defines the evaluated set as Claude 1.3, Claude 2, and Claude Instant 1.1. This predates Instant 1.2 and does not disclose its architecture or counts.

sources.title: Model Card and Evaluations for Claude Models (November 21, 2023 update)
sources.evidence: Adds a Claude 2.1 appendix while retaining the original model-details text and Instant 1.1 comparison. No Instant 1.2 parameter count or exact architecture disclosure was found.

sources.title: Claude 3 model card
sources.evidence: Later-card check attempted. The official redirect target was inaccessible, and the historical CDN PDF exceeded the web reader size limit; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403. Its content was not used as technical evidence.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Current API terms grant service access and reserve intellectual-property rights. These June 2025 terms support the descriptive proprietary service classification but are not represented as the original 2023 contract.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: Anthropic explicitly states that Claude weights are not publicly released or provided to users. This is first-party evidence about weight availability independent of the existence of a hosted API; the paper's benchmark models are newer Claude versions.

sources.title: Claude 3 family card with later addenda — full accessible copy
sources.evidence: Parent accessed the full 64-page combined PDF. Five exact Instant 1.2 references concern multilingual MMLU, QuALITY, discrimination and BBQ evaluations. Full-text searches disclose no Instant 1.2 total/active counts or architecture.

sources.title: Claude model pricing linked from the Instant 1.2 release
sources.evidence: The exact Instant 1.2 announcement links this one-page sheet, which lists the Instant offering with a 100,000-token context window.

sources.title: Releasing Claude Instant 1.2 — fresh parameter review
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact-version release identifies Instant 1.1 as predecessor and describes incorporating Claude 2 capabilities, with coding/math/safety results. It supplies neither a nominal parameter count nor an explicit relationship to a numerically sized base model; incorporating capabilities alone is insufficient for a size inference.

sources.title: Claude 2 model card with November 2023 appendix — fresh primary PDF
sources.evidence: Fresh CDN retrieval at 2026-10-27T10:08:59Z; independently inspected cached text. Section 3 names Instant 1.1, not 1.2. Figure 6 separates research preference/language-model parameter-axis curves from categorical Claude-model bars; the axis does not disclose Instant parameters. The later appendix and comparison tables provide no nominal total or activated-parameter column for Instant 1.2.

sources.title: Claude 3 combined model card and addenda — fresh primary PDF
sources.evidence: Fresh CDN retrieval at 2026-10-27T10:09:00Z; independently searched cached full text and inspected relevant passages. Exact Instant 1.2 columns in Table 5 report multilingual MMLU accuracy and Table 6 reports QuALITY accuracy. Section 7.3.1 and Figures 20–21 compare discrimination/BBQ outcomes. These are evaluation columns, not total or activated parameters; no numerical Instant 1.2 size or sized-base lineage appears.

sources.title: Collective Constitutional AI — Instant-sized research models
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the training/evaluation section. Anthropic describes two Instant-sized Public and Standard models and separately uses Claude Instant 1.2 as a control. The linked Instant-sized reference resolves to the original Claude introduction, which supplies no numerical size. The blog gives no total/active count.

sources.title: Collective Constitutional AI: Aligning a Language Model with Public Input, section 3.4
sources.evidence: Freshly read section 3.4 and checked the paper for numerical size disclosures. It explicitly states that Public, Standard and Claude Instant 1.2 share model configurations including size, architecture and pretraining data. This is a valid same-size relationship, but none of the three receives a numerical parameter count. Using the training methods from Bai et al. (2022) does not identify these later models with a particular sized model from that paper. The linked project repository documents participant-data processing, not a model-size specification.

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback — cited training-method source
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the cited paper. Figure 2 labels 52B RL runs, Figure 3 compares models of varying sizes, and section 3.3 identifies a 52B SL-CAI research model. The later Collective Constitutional AI paper cites its methods, without stating that its Public/Standard models or Instant 1.2 are this 52B model. The nominal 52B research count is valid for its stated subject but cannot be assigned to Instant 1.2.

sources.title: Measuring the persuasiveness of language models — later Instant comparison
sources.evidence: Freshly read the model comparison and footnote 5. Instant 1.2 and Haiku are successive generations in a compact model class, while other models are classed as frontier. Numerical outputs are persuasiveness scores, not parameter counts. No nominal total, activated count, or numerically sized base relationship is supplied.

name.note: Exact version named by its developer.

family.note: Claude family; Instant 1.2 is distinguished from Instant 1.1 and Claude 2.

release_date.note: Announcement explicitly says businesses can access 1.2 through the API on this date; not the earlier Instant-family launch.

open_weights.note: Anthropic explicitly states that Claude weights are not publicly released or provided to users. Exact-model sources document the commercial hosted offering; this classification uses the general distribution policy without transferring technical specifications from newer models.

license.note: Descriptive proprietary classification, supported by non-distribution of Claude weights and commercial hosted access; not a named open-weight redistribution license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh release, primary-card and named-lineage review found no nominal total count. Collective Constitutional AI explicitly establishes the same size for Instant 1.2 and its Public/Standard models, but supplies no numerical size; its citation of the CAI training method does not establish identity with a 52B research model. No exact tensor census is required for a nominal count; the missing evidence is a supported number or numerically sized lineage.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh searches for active/activated counts and inspection of later first-party comparison tables found no Instant 1.2 activated-parameter specification. Claude 3 tables report benchmark accuracy and bias outcomes, while the persuasiveness study reports scores. Neither total-equals-active nor an architectural convention is assumed.

architecture.note: The Transformer statement describes Claude 2 and previous versions, with Instant 1.1 named in the evaluated set. It is insufficient for later Instant 1.2. Exact-model first-party architecture/interpretability searches found no usable disclosure.

context_window.note: The 100,000-token context article explicitly evaluates Instant 1.2. Historical documented capacity, not evidence of an operating endpoint.

modalities.note: Release tasks and the exact-model long-document experiments establish text input and text answers.

reasoning.note: Ordinary reasoning improvements and prompted scratchpads do not establish a dedicated reasoning/thinking mode. No exact-model mode specification verified.

tool_call.note: The long-context article links a separate cookbook tool-flow demo, but does not establish native structured tool calling for Instant 1.2.

description.value: Historical Anthropic text model in the Claude Instant line, released through the API on August 9, 2023, with a 100,000-token context window. The Anthropic API model was retired on November 6, 2024.
description.note: Replaces the generic description with exact-version release, capacity and Anthropic API retirement facts.

patch.description: Historical Anthropic text model in the Claude Instant line, released through the API on August 9, 2023, with a 100,000-token context window. The Anthropic API model was retired on November 6, 2024.
patch.notes: Anthropic discloses neither a nominal total nor an active parameter count for Instant 1.2; its same-sized Collective Constitutional AI research models also have no published count. Architecture and native reasoning/tool-calling support remain unverified for this exact revision; the original Claude 2 model card discusses Instant 1.1. Anthropic retired claude-instant-1.2 on November 6, 2024; partner platforms may have separate lifecycles.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only review keeps nominal total and active counts undisclosed with explicit null patch values. Reopened the release and inspected freshly retrieved Claude 2/3 cards, including later exact-version comparison columns. Newly followed Collective Constitutional AI evidence establishes a same-size relationship with Public/Standard models but no number; the cited CAI method does not make Instant 1.2 the 52B research model. Later persuasiveness comparisons supply scores only. Other field assessments are preserved.
